paragraph: Ho-Ho-Kus is a single-family market, essentially all of it, with 37 sales over six months at a median of $1,525,000. The typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with three full baths, and prices ran from $840,000 to $4,950,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. The sale-to-list ratio sits right at 1.00 with 46 percent of homes going above asking and a median of 17 days on market. That is competitive but not frenzied. Expect competition on the good ones and room to negotiate on the rest. Volume built the way it usually does, thin in late winter and peaking with 11 closings in June, and the median easing from $1,850,000 in May to $1,400,000 in July came alongside rising volume, which reads as a shift toward more mid-range houses rather than values falling. If the usual seasonal arc holds, closings taper modestly through fall before deep winter thins out. Your real decision here is which pocket of town and how much house, not whether to wait out the market.
